contract: Pure charges from the usage totals of one tenant and period under one immutable rate-card version. price/3 takes a card {card_id, version, content_hash, kind :cost | :price, currency (a domain/money registry member with an integer minor unit), rounding (one of Elzoo.Money.rounding_modes/0), lines} of 1..1024 stand-alone lines {provider_id, model_id, unit, rate, per, minimum} sorted and unique on {provider_id, model_id, unit}, with an exact decimal-string rate (at most 18 significant and 18 fractional digits) per power-of-ten units (1..10^9) and an optional minimum, and usage {tenant, period, rows} of 0..4096 rows in the domain/metering totals shape plus provider_id and model_id; a usage prices only when each row's key {provider_id, model_id, unit} has a card line, so at most 3 x the card's lines rows (3072 with 1024 lines), a larger usage unpriced_unit. Each line with a row is charged quantity x rate / per, built exactly in integer arithmetic and rounded once through Elzoo.Money.from_decimal/4, then raised to its minimum; a line with no row is absent; unknown observations add nothing to quantity, count in unknown_count and make the charge incomplete, never priced as zero. A charge {tenant, period, card identity, lines, total, incomplete, unknown_count} has an exact total in the card currency. difference/3 is later.total - earlier.total for two charges of one tenant, period and card identity. Both take opts [] (the compiled domain/money registry) or [registry: r], r the compiled default, a raw domain/money registry or a checked value of Elzoo.Money.Registry.check/1; a raw registry is checked once per call with check/1 and that checked value goes to every domain/money call of the call, a checked value as it is; a registry that check/1 refuses, a forged checked value included, is invalid. content_hash/1 is the SHA-256 of a documented canonical card encoding. Fixed error atoms in the order invalid, card, content_hash, usage, unpriced_unit, amount_range, and charge, card_mismatch for difference/3; none echoes an ID or amount. Kind, source and error sets and the returned maps may gain members. No I/O, clock, storage, journal post, tiers, exchange rate, invoice or Float.
limits: No tiers, exchange rate, tax, discount, invoice, payment or journal post; the README states how a host posts a charge or a correction difference as a domain/journal post/3 operation.
One currency per card; a tenant billed in two currencies uses two cards, and a tenant with two plans whose cards cover different usage prices each subset with its own card.
Rates are owner-authored; llm_db prices are a reference only.
The charge of an incomplete line covers its known amounts only.
An exact line value must fit 38 significant digits (with an 18-fractional-digit rate per unit, a quantity below about 10^20); a larger one is amount_range, never truncated.

The per-provider and per-model rows come from Elzoo.Metering.model_totals/3 of domain/metering for a period of at most 1,000 groups (max_rows 1..1000; more groups than max_rows is read_limit), and the host builds the rows of a larger period, up to 4096 rows, of which at most 3 x the card's lines (3072 with 1024 lines) can be priced; the Piece does not check that the rows are a complete period, and the host owns the period and the card choice.

The cost per call of each registry: form, price/3 of one unchanged 1024-line card and usage with a row and a minimum on every line, accepted by all three forms with equal charges, three runs in one local session on the pinned toolchain (ELZ-321; mean of 30 calls after 5 warm-up; local timings, not a bound); the custom registry is the default's extract with only its downloaded header changed (the same version and entries, one version of 307 entries, not === the default): opts [] (the compiled default, one === comparison where each domain/money call resolves its registry: option) 16.74, 18.39 and 18.28 ms; a checked value of the custom registry 20.84, 18.96 and 19.50 ms, one constant-time test where each domain/money call resolves its registry: option and one in each unwrap of the positional lookups that member/2 makes (held?/2, entry/3); the same registry as a raw map 19.40, 17.58 and 19.10 ms, one check/1 walk per call (domain/money states about 65-80 microseconds) and then as a checked value; an explicit compiled default is sealed by check/1 and costs as a checked value. Passing the raw map to every domain/money call again measured 203.97, 206.64 and 201.59 ms in that session; that the walk is once per call is grounded by this measurement, not by a test.

Selected Cure laws cover the minimum and completeness decisions in decision-split form, taking the below decision and the per-line known flags as arguments; that is_below and is_zero compute them from the integers is test-grounded, as are validation, the exact value, rounding (domain/money's), the content hash and the error order, which are Elixir-side.

grounding.claim: For every rounded charge and minimum, a line with a row and a minimum whose below decision (rounded < minimum) is True is charged the minimum (decision-split form).

For every rounded charge and minimum, a line with a row and a minimum whose below decision is False keeps its rounded charge; with minimum_floor, a charged line with a minimum is at least the minimum given that the production is_below decision is rounded < minimum, which rests on pinned Cure Int comparison and the production-decision tests, not on a law.
For every below decision, a line with a row and no minimum keeps its rounded charge.
For every minimum flag and decision, a line with no row is LineAbsent (not charged).
For all earlier and later line flags, one line whose unknown count is not zero (flag False) makes all_known False, so the charge is incomplete (induction on the earlier lines).
A charge with no line is complete.

Pinned Cure checks the PricingLine verdict and the production line/4 and complete/1 decisions (every function @total) with a clean audit: no axioms, holes, unresolved, unaudited, opaque or unproven-total items.

Listed scenarios with hand-written expected amounts: EUR, JPY and BHD cards; 18-fractional-digit rates (half_up and down), per 1 and 10^6; a cache-write line; two providers and two models of one unit apart; the seven rounding modes at half a minor unit (0.5 and 1.5 cents), just above and below it and on a whole 7 cents; a caller Decimal context of precision 2 not applied; two rows of 0.4 cents in two sources charged 1 cent once per line; known 0 charged the minimum or zero; a card line with no row absent also with a minimum; charges above, at and below the minimum; empty usage complete with a zero total; known and unknown rows charging the known amount with unknown_count and incomplete; all-unknown lines charged the minimum or zero and incomplete; one incomplete line making the charge incomplete; unpriced_unit also for an all-unknown row; a version 1 charge equal after version 2; difference card_mismatch for versions, kinds, tenants, periods and currencies; content_hash mismatch, content_hash/1 ignoring its key and distinguishing every body field; fixed hand-written encoding bytes and a pinned SHA-256; corrections up (+15.00 EUR), down (-2.00 EUR) and equal (0); mixed units and models unpriced; duplicate and unsorted lines; the fixed error order (an unpriced row before an amount_range line); options, including registries that Elzoo.Money.Registry.check/1 refuses (a forged four-key map, empty versions, a checked struct holding a test closure); a checked value of a two-version registry pricing both charges and their difference equal to its raw registry; rates -1, 01, 1., .5, 1e3, a Float, an integer, 19 significant and 19 fractional digits; per 0, 3, 10^10; minimums finer than the minor unit, negative and non-string; forged, unit-less and non-struct currencies; versions 0 and 2^31, kinds, roundings; lines 0, 1024 and 1025, improper lists and extra keys; rows 4096 and 4097, count 0, 3072 rows on a full 1024-line card priced and 3073 unpriced_unit, unknown_count above count, known above 0 with every observation unknown, known 10^38; each text at 0, 128 and 129 bytes (128-byte row IDs priced), invalid UTF-8, C0, DEL and C1; a 39-digit exact coefficient amount_range and a 38-digit one priced; known 10^37 at rate 100000000000000000 per 1 (exponent 54) amount_range; a result and a total past the domain/money range amount_range; a trailing-zero coefficient trimmed before the bound; difference refusing malformed charges including a negative total; junk inputs without a raise. Pricing unknown as zero with the charge complete fails the unknown cases and rounding each row before summing a line fails the once-per-line case; letting a below-minimum charge keep its rounded value fails minimum_floor at compile and letting an unknown flag pass fails incomplete_when_unknown at compile; taking any checked struct unchecked fails the options case and pricing a checked value under the default fails the checked-registry case (negative controls). Finite scenarios, not universal proofs.
Pinned Cure compilation, reduction checking, audit and BEAM decision semantics; compiler soundness not locally proved.
Decimal 3.2.0 Decimal.new/3 builds the exact struct (sign, coef, exp) that domain/money from_decimal/4 reads field by field; no Decimal arithmetic or context is used.
Pinned Elixir/OTP integer arithmetic, Erlang term order of binaries, atoms and tuples for the line order, Regex anchors, String.valid?/1 and the utf8 binary pattern.
OTP 29.1.2 :crypto SHA-256 of the canonical card encoding gives the content hash.

The host stores each card version unchanged with its content hash and the card identity with each charge, re-prices an earlier charge only under its own card version, supplies the complete per-provider and per-model rows of the period, read with domain/metering model_totals/3 or built, and posts charges and nonzero differences to domain/journal itself.

telemetry.contract: Pure functions emit no observations and no logs; the host owns instrumentation.

config.contract: Fixed Contract bounds (1..1024 lines, 0..4096 rows of which at most 3 x the card's lines price, 128-byte texts, versions 1..2^31-1, rates of 18 significant and 18 fractional digits, per 1..10^9, known 0..10^38-1); the card, usage and registry: option are per-call operands, not settings.
